Problem: Suspected lower GI cancer -- FIT declined by patient -- 2WW referral submitted by clinical judgement.

History: 38-year-old man presents with a five-week history of fresh rectal bleeding, almost daily, mixed with stool, and a clear change in bowel habit (looser stools, three to four per day, from a baseline of one daily). He reports mild lower abdominal cramping that is partly relieved by defaecation. He has lost approximately 3kg. Family history: father diagnosed with colorectal cancer at age 49, paternal aunt with bowel cancer in her 60s.

Faecal immunochemical test: the patient was offered FIT testing today and at the previous appointment two weeks ago. He has FIT declined on both occasions -- he explained that he is unable to manage the home sample kit due to a sensory aversion and a history of OCD that makes the home collection process intolerable for him. He is willing to proceed directly to endoscopic investigation. The FIT declined status is documented for the specialist's awareness; no FIT positive (or otherwise) result is available because the test was not performed in this episode. The phrase "FIT positive" appears on the local 2WW proforma template only as a tick-box prompt for clinicians; it is NOT a result for this patient.

Plan: 2WW lower GI referral submitted today on clinical grounds (rectal bleeding, change in bowel habit, weight loss, strong family history). Patient counselled and aware that this is a suspected cancer referral. Safety-net advice given.

Examination: Soft abdomen, no organomegaly, no palpable mass. DRE: no rectal mass; small internal haemorrhoids only.

Decision to refer: 2026-05-18.
